title: The Most Effective Teaching Style
author: Michel Delving
summary: The article argues that the most effective teaching style is not a universal method but whatever approach the teacher can deliver with the most consistent enthusiasm — a claim grounded in fifteen years of classroom experience. Drawing on his own persistent pre-class nerves, author Michel Delving frames teaching as a performance discipline in which method matters far less than delivery conviction. He outlines five major teaching styles — lecture, demonstration, project-based, gamification, and blended — each with distinct strengths and ideal contexts. Lecture earns a particularly strong defense: passivity, not the format itself, is the failure mode, and vocal variety with embedded questioning makes teacher-led instruction deeply engaging. Gamification targets the dopaminergic system to manufacture excitement, which Delving treats as a legitimate tool rather than a shallow gimmick. Blended teaching, combining multiple styles within a single lesson through real-time improvisation, is identified as the hallmark of master teachers. The article implicitly pushes back against prescriptive pedagogy: any sound method executed with genuine investment will outperform a theoretically superior one delivered halfheartedly.
points: The 'most effective' teaching style is the one the teacher can sustain enthusiastically — method matters less than delivery conviction, meaning any sound pedagogical approach executed with genuine investment will outperform a theoretically superior style executed halfheartedly.

Lecture is not inherently passive: voice inflection, strategic questioning, and chunked information delivery can make teacher-led instruction deeply engaging, reversing the common assumption that lecture is an outmoded format.

Gamification targets the dopaminergic system — giving short bursts of excitement or promoting addiction to class time — which makes it a legitimate engagement tool rather than merely a trendy gimmick.
Blended teaching, combining multiple styles in a single lesson, requires real-time improvisation beyond what can be planned, distinguishing master practitioners from merely competent ones.

Even persistent teacher nerves — described as quadrupled at the start of a new semester — signal investment rather than weakness, and Delving frames pre-class anxiety as a functional check on complacency rather than a problem to eliminate.
quotes: The reality is that the most effectively teaching style is whatever style you are able to do with the most consistent amount of enthusiasm you can muster. Teaching is a grind. After 15 years in the trenches, I still get nervous every time I see students walking in for class.

If you perform lecture-style teaching with passion and mindfulness, it is an excellent style of teaching. Voice inflection can be a crucial tool to keep kids engaged and attentive. We all had that monotone teacher who seemed to be trying to put kids to sleep.
Sometimes you just need to info-dump. Sometimes you just need to talk it out. Sometimes kids just want to be put into the hypnotic rhythm of a good lecture.

Not all lectures are built the same. You want your lectures to be active as opposed to passive. Break streams of information into manageable chunks that also (at effective times) require student participation.

USE QUESTIONS! The human brain is wired to automatically begin formulating answers when questions are directly posed to it. Even if students don't raise their hands or their voices to participate, the gears may be turning in their heads.

Gamification seeks to hijack students' dopaminergic systems for effective learning. Anything that gives short bursts of excitement or seeks to promote addiction to class time or learning is part of this teaching style.

This is a student-centered approach wherein the teacher serves as a guide or mentor while students work through the process of knowledge or skill accumulation for themselves. Often, an important component of project-based teaching is peer-to-peer interaction. Students often find the answers or develop the skills through a process of exploration.

The best teachers with an exceptional grasp of many different teaching styles know when and how to make changes on the fly so learning continues to happen in efficient, potent, and streamlined ways even when things happen that could not be fully planned for.
